The other top-level *.md and a few docs/*.md are WORKING / DESIGN notes written while building features. Many describe features that are now DONE (merged into code + USER_GUIDE + ROADMAP), so the note is redundant scratch. Some may still hold open items not captured anywhere.
docs/archive/ already holds superseded docs (commercial_v1_roadmap.md, driver_ROADMAP.md, TODO.md).

YOU ARE AUDITING ONE DOC (READ-ONLY - do not edit, move, or delete any file): `cosim_roi.md`

Steps:
1. Read `cosim_roi.md` fully. Note its topic and any status it self-declares (DONE/SUPERSEDED/REMOVED/etc).
2. VERIFY the real status against the codebase - do not trust the doc:
   - `git log --oneline -- <relevant paths>` and `git log --oneline --all -S '<keyword>'` for the feature it describes.
   - Search ROADMAP.md for the matching feature id / FR row and its Status (done/partial/not-started/REMOVED).
   - Search docs/USER_GUIDE.md for whether the feature is documented for users.
   - Search docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb for related L-ids.
   - Confirm the implementation + tests actually exist in the tree (grep code).
3. Decide verified_status: done (implemented, tested, in USER_GUIDE/ROADMAP) | partial | open | stale-superseded | canonical-keep | unknown.
4. List content_absorbed_in: where the doc's info now lives. If the feature is DONE and fully captured in code+USER_GUIDE+ROADMAP, the doc is redundant.
5. List open_items the doc still records, and for EACH say whether it is already_tracked_in ROADMAP (feature id) or limitations (L-id) or NOT-tracked, and the route (limitations-notebook / TODO / roadmap / already-tracked / none).
6. recommendation:
   - delete: feature DONE and fully absorbed; doc is pure redundant scratch with NO untracked open items.
   - extract-then-delete: doc has open items NOT tracked anywhere - they must be routed to limitations/TODO/roadmap first, then the doc can go.
   - archive: historical value (a removed-feature rationale, a superseded plan worth keeping for provenance) -> move to docs/archive/.
   - keep: still an active/canonical reference.
Be concrete in evidence (real commit hashes, file paths, section names). Return ONLY the structured object.

1	# cosim_roi -- checkpoint co-simulation between QEMU and vsim inside the ROI
2	
3	Status: ACCEPTED (PM decision, 2026-06-12): Option A (checkpoint co-sim).
4	  1. Dev tier (debug tool, hidden from release help like state-diff).
5	  2. Default checkpoint interval N=10000; `--cosim-interval <N>` overrides.
6	  3. Trigger scope: marker|pc only (same as --verify).
7	
8	## Problem
9	
10	`--verify` (verify_oracle.md) compares only the FINAL state at the ROI exit.
11	When it fails, we know the vsim leg diverged somewhere inside the ROI, but not
12	where. Checkpoint co-sim drains and compares the architectural state every N
13	retired instructions, so a divergence is localized to the first bad
14	N-instruction window. Rerun with smaller N to narrow it.
15	
16	## Flow
17	
18	```
19	Run 1 (hybrid):  QEMU1 -> vsim: ..N insns..|..N insns..|.. exit
20	                                  ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final drain
21	Run 2 (oracle):  pure QEMU from boot: arm at ROI entry, drain at the SAME
22	                 retire counts ->     ckpt 1      ckpt 2      final
23	diff ckpt k vs ckpt k (existing state_diff policy); first mismatch = window k.
24	```
25	
26	Alignment is by RETIRE COUNT, not pc: vsim's DMI halt overshoots 0-3
27	instructions (halt slack, see verify_oracle.md "Boundary semantics"), and pc
28	alignment is ambiguous inside loops. vsim restores minstret from QEMU1's
29	drained value at entry, so `ckpt.minstret - entry.minstret` is the exact
30	number of post-entry retires; the oracle plugin counts exec callbacks after
31	arming and drains at those exact deltas. pc then matches by construction
32	when execution is correct, and diverges loudly when it is not.
33	
34	## Memory: keep the mmap Shared, do NOT flip to Private
35	
36	- Today: QEMU writes guest RAM through `-object memory-backend-file,share=on`;
37	  vsim maps the same file `MAP_SHARED | MAP_POPULATE`
38	  (verilator/src/platform/mmap_backing.hpp:34). This stays unchanged.
39	- vsim Private, QEMU shared: Linux private file mappings are copy-on-write
40	  PER PAGE; un-written pages still show the live file, so the other engine's
41	  stores leak in until the first local write. Nondeterministic contamination.
42	- QEMU Private (share=off): pre-ROI writes never reach the file; vsim resumes
43	  on stale memory. The handoff breaks.
44	- Resolution: the two runs never share memory at all. The oracle is a
45	  separate QEMU process re-running the same ELF from boot on its own RAM
46	  (exactly like --verify); pre-ROI determinism is already proven by the
47	  VERIFY=1 gate (35/35 identical entry states).
48	
49	## Design notes (from code reading)
50	
51	- vsim exit drain today: simulator.hpp check_hybrid_handoff -> on_retire(pc)
52	  -> StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough -> write file -> exit 200. Abstract
53	  reads are non-destructive, BUT the trailing V data sweep (vse8.v via the
54	  Program Buffer) clobbers vtype/vl/vstart and x5/x6/x7. The exit drain never
55	  resumes, so the clobbers are free. A CHECKPOINT drain resumes, so it must
56	  undo them from the freshly drained values (vsetvl restore staging x5/x6,
57	  then vstart, then rewrite x5/x6/x7), then resumereq + poll allresumeack.
58	  All primitives exist (resume_driver.hpp, program_buffer.hpp).
59	- Known risks (empirical, the F4 gate decides):
60	  - minstret during debug mode: if Program Buffer instructions (V sweep +
61	    clobber undo) increment minstret, later checkpoints' deltas inflate and
62	    the oracle drains late. Fix if observed: set dcsr.stopcount at halt.
63	    Non-V fixtures are clean either way (abstract commands only).
64	  - mcycle during the checkpoint halts inflates window_cycles (observed:
65	    22530 for a 1692-retire ROI); the driver therefore suppresses the
66	    window_cycles line under --cosim -- the two are mutually exclusive
67	    (PM decision 2026-06-12). Re-run without --cosim to measure.
68	
69	## F1: vsim resumable checkpoint drain
70	State: done
71	Description: `StateDrain::drain_checkpoint(input)` -- drain_with_passthrough,
72	then (V flag only) undo the sweep clobbers using the drained values:
73	stage x5=vl, x6=vtype, exec `vsetvl x0,x5,x6` in the Program Buffer, write
74	vstart (after vsetvl: vsetvl zeroes it), rewrite x5/x6/x7 from the drained
75	GPRs; finally resumereq + poll allresumeack. Hart continues where it halted
76	(DPC untouched). Unit tests on the recording-bus double assert the write
77	sequence and that the returned state equals the plain drain.
78	Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp,
79	verilator/tests/hybrid/state_drain.test.cpp
80	Dependencies: none
81	
82	## F2: vsim --hybrid-cosim N (checkpoint loop + numbered files)
83	State: done
84	Description: HandoffController counts retires; every N (monotonic target, not
85	modulo) it calls drain_checkpoint and hands the state to a sink callback;
86	the exit trigger still wins on the same retire and keeps today's semantics.
87	simulator.hpp provides the sink: V-merge from scratch (read_v_from_scratch)
88	then write `<handoff_out>.ckpt<k>` (k from 1). New CLI arg `--hybrid-cosim
89	<N>` (main.cpp), valid only with --resume-from-qemu + marker/pc trigger
90	(error with --hybrid-icount). Controller unit tests with a fake trigger +
91	recording bus; manual two-leg smoke (QEMU1 then vsim --hybrid-cosim) checks
92	.ckpt files appear with ascending minstret.
93	Key files: verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp, verilator/src/simulator.hpp,
94	verilator/src/main.cpp, verilator/tests/hybrid/handoff_controller.test.cpp
95	Dependencies: F1
96	
97	## F3: plugin cosim oracle mode (counted multi-drain)
98	State: done
99	Description: new plugin args, exclusive with all other trigger modes:
100	  cosim_marker=1      arm on the ENTER marker `slti x0,x0,0x5A0`
101	  cosim_pc=0x...      arm on an explicit entry boundary vaddr
102	  cosim_counts=a:b:c  ascending post-entry retire deltas (colon-separated);
103	                      each but the last drains to `<outfile>.ckpt<k>` and
104	                      continues; the LAST drains to `<outfile>` and exits 200
105	Counting: exec callbacks fire pre-execution; at the m-th post-arm callback
106	exactly m-1 post-entry instructions have retired, so drain when the running
107	count equals the target (check-then-increment), capturing pc = next-insn
108	vaddr -- the same point as vsim's DPC. The entry marker itself is counted by
109	NEITHER side (QEMU1 drains pre-marker, vsim resumes past it).
110	Key files: qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c,
111	tests/plugin/test_plugin_cosim_drain.sh (new)
112	Dependencies: none
113	
114	## F4: andes-sim run --cosim (default off, Dev)
115	State: done
116	Description: `--cosim` on `run --model hybrid --trigger marker|pc` (+
117	`--cosim-interval <N>`, default 10000; --cosim-interval without --cosim,
118	--cosim with fast/cycle/icount, and --cosim with --verify are usage errors;
119	--cosim already subsumes the final-state check). Flow: hybrid plan runs with
120	the vsim leg carrying `--hybrid-cosim N` (Trigger param -> leg_trigger_args);
121	run_plan collects `<outfile>.ckpt<k>` into PhaseResult.checkpoints before
122	workdir cleanup; the driver computes minstret deltas vs the entry state,
123	runs the one-step oracle plan (fresh mmap, cosim_marker/cosim_pc +
124	cosim_counts), diffs ckpt k vs ckpt k then final vs final via diff_states,
125	and reports `[cosim] PASS: <K> checkpoints + final state match` or the first
126	diverging window `[cosim] FAIL: divergence in window <k> (retires <lo>..<hi>
127	after entry)` plus the field diffs, rc 1.
128	Gate: cosim e2e green on rt_c_hello (no V), rt_c_matmul (FP), rt_c_v_regs +
129	rt_c_v_matmul (V) -- this empirically settles the minstret/debug-mode risk.
130	Key files: driver/cli.hpp/.cpp, driver/plan.hpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
131	driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/main.cpp (dev help),
132	tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_cosim.sh (new)
133	Dependencies: F1, F2, F3 (and F2's state-diff core from verify_oracle)
134	
135	## Docs
136	Each feature updates docs/USER_GUIDE.md in its own change set: F3 adds the
137	plugin-arg rows (2.3), F4 adds the dev-facing --cosim subsection next to
138	--verify (what it localizes, the masking rule, why window_cycles is
139	approximate under --cosim).
140	
141	## Rejected: Option B (streaming trace-compare)
142	Both engines stream per-retire records into shm rings; exact localization but
143	vsim's retire hook is pc-only (`on_retire(uint64_t pc)`, simulator.hpp:504; no
144	RVFI/writeback trace), so full value compare needs new RTL probing. Revisit
145	only if window-bracketing proves too coarse.
